problems.title: The released Gaussian KL halves the log-variance term
problems.source_location: Appendix A.2, PDF p.28, Eq.(8); vittle_llama.py, lines 252–289; repository issue #1
claim: The paper’s Gaussian KL is correct, but `vib_kld_loss` and `vib_kld_loss_lp` use half the required additive log-variance ratio.
analysis: At zero means, posterior variance \(1/2\), prior variance \(1\), the release returns \(-0.0767132\) instead of \(0.0965736\), within its clamps. At matching log variance \(s=0\), its derivative is \(1/4\) instead of zero; the fixed-prior minimum shifts to variance \(1/2\). The learned-prior mismatch was already raised in repository issue #1 on 28 January 2026.
result: The later release computes neither the stated KL values nor gradients. Original checkpoint training is not identified.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a known-context later-code discrepancy, not a refutation of the correct printed KL or original results.
problems.existing_correction_status: Repository issue #1 already identifies the learned-prior coefficient mismatch; no author adoption of this correction is established.

problems.title: Sequence length does not identify modality positions
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF p.5; Appendix A.2, PDF pp.28–29; vittle_arch.py packing and vittle_llama.py, lines 312–334 and 439–490
claim: The public packing path replaces image sentinels in place, while the bottleneck route infers a visual prefix from total-length subtraction.
analysis: IDs \([1,2,\mathrm{image},3,4]\) expanded with visual rows \([101,102,103]\) become \([1,2,101,102,103,3,4]\). True visual indices are \(\{2,3,4\}\), but the inferred count \(7-5=2\) selects prefix \(\{0,1\}\), both text. Replacing one sentinel increases length by \(n-1\), not \(n\), even when the image is first. Embedding-only input sets the inferred visual count to zero in the inspected branch.
result: The public route does not implement the intended modality split. Full intended-version generation behavior and benchmark effects are unmeasured.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Carry an explicit visual-token mask through expansion, padding, truncation and cached generation; exclude padding separately.
problems.impact_rationale: This is later released modality routing, without established central original-result damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The skip contribution breaks the common-latent lower bound
problems.source_location: Eqs.(2)–(5), PDF p.4; Section 3.3 and footnote 2, PDF p.5; Implication paragraph, PDF p.6; Appendix D, PDF p.38
claim: Section 3.2 introduces Eq.(4) as a variational IB lower bound and Eq.(5) as its empirical estimate. The implemented likelihood receives \(\hat Z=(1-\alpha)c(X)+\alpha\tilde Z\), while the KL regularizes unmixed \(\tilde Z\). Footnote 2 and Appendix D explicitly acknowledge the different laws, yet the p.6 Implication paragraph still says that Vittle maximizes the variational IB lower bound.
analysis: Let \(X=\pm2\) equally, label \(Y\) constant, \(c(X)=X\), and \(\tilde Z\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) matching its prior independently of \(X\). At \(\alpha=1/2\), the mixed objective is zero for a decoder assigning the sole label probability one. Yet \(\hat Z\mid X=\pm2\sim\mathcal N(\pm1,1/4)\), so \(I(X;\hat Z)>0\), while \(I(Y;\hat Z)=0\). The actual information-bottleneck value is \(-\beta I(X;\hat Z)<0\), so zero is above rather than below it. A finite-softmax likelihood arbitrarily close to zero preserves the strict contradiction.
result: The stated auxiliary-KL objective is not a general lower bound for the representation actually decoded. A useful auxiliary regularizer remains a different interpretation.
assumptions: The posterior Gaussian has positive variance, the prior is input-independent, and the decoder actually receives the interpolated representation.
repair: Use the same mixed law \(\mathcal N((1-\alpha)c+\alpha\mu,\alpha^2\operatorname{diag}\sigma^2)\) in likelihood and KL to an input-independent prior, with any modality-factorization assumptions explicit.
problems.impact_rationale: Despite its explicit disclosure of asymmetric posterior laws, the paper still asserts the lower-bound interpretation for Vittle on p.6. The admissible nondegenerate Gaussian construction contradicts that central variational claim; usefulness as an auxiliary regularizer is not refuted.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Conditional independence does not eliminate input-shift residuals
problems.source_location: Proposition 3.2 and interpretation after Eq.(7), PDF p.6; Appendix E.2, PDF pp.39–41
claim: After Proposition 3.2, the interpretation drops \(\Delta_{X\mid Z}\) because model output is conditionally independent of input given the representation.
analysis: Let domain \(P\) concentrate on input \(a\), and \(Q\) be uniform on \(b,c\). Use one label kernel: a fair label at \(a\), label zero at \(b\), label one at \(c\). Let latents be domain-identical and input-independent, and model output a fair independent label. Conditional independence holds; all retained latent-divergence and marginal entropy-gap terms are zero. True mutual information changes from zero to \(\log2\), so EMID is \(\log2\). The residual is \(2\log2\); retaining it leaves the full proposition uncontradicted. Lowering model entropy can also enlarge an absolute gap to a fixed fair-target entropy.
result: Only the deletion/monotonic interpretation fails; the full printed bound survives this example.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Retain the residual unless conditional input laws agree across domains on the relevant representation fibres. Keep entropy terms as absolute gaps rather than assuming lower model entropy always improves them.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an overstrong interpretation of a valid full bound, rather than a direct contradiction of that bound.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
